rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: While traveling, the Prophet sought God’s protection from the land, its inhabitants and creatures, including snakes and scorpions.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm sefere çıkıp da bir menzile konduğu zaman şöyle derdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The travel supplication contains no indication of blowing; Qur’anic commands to pray and seek refuge suffice to establish its legitimacy, while the Prophet’s own blowing and wiping are also established.
rows.anchor: Bunlarda üflemeye dair bir işaret yoktur. Ve bunların meşrûiyeti için başka delîle hâcet olmaksızın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet customarily recited the Muʿawwidhāt nightly, blew into his hands, and wiped his face and body.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah her gece Mu‘avvizât’ı okur ellerine üfler, yüzüne ve cesedine meshederdi

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha says the Prophet blew the Muʿawwidhāt over ill family members; during his final illness she recited and blew over him, then used his own hand to wipe him because it was more blessed.
rows.anchor: yine Hazret-i Âişe’den sıhâhta mervîdir ki: “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ehlinden birisi hastalandığı vakit

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet rubbed the ill with his right hand and prayed for healing; when she tried this during his final illness, he withdrew his hand and prayed to join the highest companion before dying.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe demiştir ki: “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bizden bir insan rahatsız olduğu vakit onu sağ eliyle mesheder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet sometimes healed wounded people immediately by reciting and touching them, but these were prophetic miracles and do not prove the same effect for others.
rows.anchor: onun nübüvveti havâssından olan mu‘cizât kabîlinden olduğu için diğerleri hakkında istidlâl olunmaz

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet permitted ruqya for a household among the Anṣār after a venomous creature such as a scorpion stung someone; the report supports Jabir’s accounts.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ensardan bir ehl-i beyte humeden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since sucking a sting is medically useful, spitting during treatment may also have a rationale; ruqya for the evil eye is reported, and its psychological nature makes spiritual suggestion’s benefit evident.
rows.anchor: bunda emmek tıbben de müfîd olduğuna göre tükürmenin de bir vechi mülâhaza edilebilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruqya with transmitted prayers for spiritual or bodily well-being is permissible absent sorcery, but asking another to recite is not religiously commendable because it seeks an intermediary; the most favored servants avoid it.
rows.anchor: Allah’a sığınmak ve dua etmek için başkasının tavassutunu dilenmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hanafi law, treatment is unobjectionable when one believes God alone heals and makes medicine a means; it is impermissible to believe the medicine itself heals.
rows.anchor: Şâfî ancak Allah teâlâ olduğuna ve devâyı ona sebep kıldığına itikad ettiği takdirde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causes that remove harm fall into certain means, such as water for thirst and bread for hunger; abandoning a certain means is not reliance on God and is unlawful when death is feared.
rows.anchor: Birincisi maktû‘un bihtir: Susuzluk zararını gideren su ve açlık zararını gideren ekmek gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjectural means such as ruqya are best left as an expression of reliance on God, since the Prophet describes the reliant as not seeking ruqya.
rows.anchor: Üçüncüsü de mevhumdur, rukye gibi. İmdi maktû‘un bih olanın terki tevekkülden değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Probable medical means such as cupping, bloodletting and purgatives do not conflict with reliance on God; their use is not obligatory to avoid, and sometimes omission is preferable depending on the person and circumstances.
rows.anchor: etıbbâ indindeki esbâb-ı zâhire ile müdâvat böyledir, bunu yapmak tevekküle münâfî değildir

rows.speaker: Atâ, Mücâhid ve Ebû Kılâbe
rows.claim: Atā, Mujāhid and Abū Qilāba permit Qur’anic ruqya for the sick or stung, including reciting over them, writing a text to hang, or washing ink from a bowl to drink.
rows.anchor: Atâ, Mücâhid ve Ebû Kılâbe mubah olduğuna

rows.speaker: Nehaî ve Basrî
rows.claim: Al-Naḵhaʿī and al-Baṣrī regard Qur’anic ruqya practices such as recitation, hanging written text, or drinking washed ink as disliked.
rows.anchor: Nehaî ve Basrî kerâhetine kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite the disagreement, Qur’anic ruqya became established in prominent practice without being rejected.
rows.anchor: fakat meşâhîrde inkâr edilmeyerek sâbit de olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A talisman is allowed, but should be removed in the lavatory and during sexual intimacy.
rows.anchor: Ta‘vîz, yani muska takınmakta beis yoktur velâkin halâda ve mukārenet zamanında çıkarır

rows.speaker: Câmi‘u’s-Sağīr
rows.claim: The cited legal source rules that commissioning a talisman so that an unwilling spouse will love the wearer is forbidden.
rows.anchor: bir kadın kocası sevmediği için sevsin diye muska yaptırmak isterse Câmi‘u’s-Sağīr’de der ki bu haramdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling ruqya conjectural does not mean baseless or false; it means its probability is weaker than certainty and dominant presumption, below even fifty percent.
rows.anchor: mevhum denilmekten murad da hiç aslı yok yalan demek değil, “maktû‘”un ve zann-ı gālib demek olan “maznun”un mukabili

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Medical knowledge remains empirical and uncertain, so this three-part classification still applies; even highly reliable remedies are probabilistic, and some conditions may improve through ruqya when medicine fails.
rows.anchor: hayâtın, emrâzın tam bir hudûdu çizilmiş olmadığı gibi fennî tedavi de ampirik olmaktan çıkarılmış değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible benefit with no corresponding risk should not be forbidden: even a very small evidence-based prospect may be used when needed and no stronger option exists.
rows.anchor: Mukabilinde bir şer ve zarar melhuz olmadıkça mümkin olan en zayıf bir fâide ihtimâlinden dahi insanları men‘etmek doğru olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people are especially liable to fall into sorcerers’ and devils’ influence amid uncertain situations, possible harms also require careful consideration.
rows.anchor: insanların sihirbazlara, şeytanlara kapılması da en ziyade bu gibi şüpheli ahvâl içinde vukū‘a gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legal epistemology makes certain evidence binding in belief and action; presumptive evidence does not compel belief but compels action when needed, while doubt counts only when useful for precaution.
rows.anchor: kat‘î delil ile itikad ve amel vâcibdir, hilâfına kavî delil bulunmayan zannî delil ile itikad vâcib olmasa da inde’l-hâce amel vâcib olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applied to treatment, certain means must be used and may not be abandoned when harm is feared; probable means are permissible, with use or omission sometimes preferable, while conjectural means are allowed but better left.
rows.anchor: şifâ Allah’tan bilinmek şartıyla tedavinin kat‘î olanıyla amel vâcib, inde’l-havf terki haram

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruqya is classed as conjectural because efficacy is attributed to the reciter’s breath, not because it is a prayer.
rows.anchor: Mevhum olmasının sebebi de dua olması itibariyle değil, okuyanın nefesinde sebebiyet mülâhazası itibariyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruqya is only a concession, not a religious duty; the pious response is to leave it, trust God, seek refuge directly, and avoid requesting another person’s intercession.
rows.anchor: halkın pek çoğunun zannettiği gibi dindarlığın îcâbı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ prayers for one another, in their presence or absence, are lawful, commendable and a religious duty; prayer is worship’s core, but praying differs from blowing and expecting help from another’s breath.
rows.anchor: Mü’minin mü’mine gerek huzûrunda ve gerek gıyâbında duası meşrû‘ve müstahsen ve hatta vazîfe-i dîniyesi bulunduğunda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands direct supplication, promises response and nearness, and forbids associating another with Him; Qur’an and prophetic teaching give the best prayers, and these suras command direct refuge.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ duayı emretmiş, ٱدْعُونِىٓ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should memorize these prayers, recite them sincerely and cleanly every night or when needed, blow over themselves, pray for fellow believers, and acknowledge the blessing of others’ sincere prayers.
rows.anchor: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den mervî olduğu üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking a prayer-broker because one will not address God directly is a pre-Islamic custom, not a requirement of piety.
rows.anchor: dua dellâlı aramaya ve onun nefesinden meded ummaya kalkışmak diyânetin îcâbı değil câhiliye âdetidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the phrase as women who blow on knots, meaning deceitful women who use stratagems.
rows.anchor: düğümlere üfleyen kadınlar, اَلنِّسَاءُ الْكَيَّادَاتُ yani hîlebaz kadınlar

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim
rows.claim: Abū Muslim interprets the phrase as women who entice men by displaying their charms and stirring them into temptation; Rāzī calls this view attractive but notes its difference from most exegetes.
rows.anchor: Râzî’nin beyânına göre Ebû Müslim bu sonuncuyu ihtiyar eylemiştir

rows.speaker: Ebû Müslim
rows.claim: On this reading, knots are resolve and deliberation, while blowing is metaphorical softening: women’s excitement and influence turn men from one judgment or resolve to another.
rows.anchor: Bu surette “ukde” azîmet, yani akd-i kalb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seductive-women interpretation fits the broad ordinary and lexical sense of sorcery and is one aspect of the more general reference to sorcerers and sorceresses.
rows.anchor: bu kavil de ondan hâriç değil, onun bir vechi demek olur

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ ve bazı ârifîn
rows.claim: They interpret the puffers as souls or powers, especially plant-like organic powers that govern growth and nutrition and underlie bodily and sexual desire; this is broader than the earlier readings.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ’nın ve bazı ârifînin ihtiyar eylediği vecihtir ki ukdelere üfleyen nefisler

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Ibn Sīnā reads the darkening one as the animal power: a murky, dark force, unlike the pristine rational soul, which is free of material attachments and able to receive forms and truths.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ “gāsik”ı kuvve-i hayvâniyeye

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Plant powers puff into three bodily dimensions—length, breadth and depth; breathing is literal in plant life, and knots may literally refer to plants’ nodes.
rows.anchor: ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ da kuvve-i hayvâniyenin şartı olan kuvâ-yı nebatiyeye işarettir

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Animality mediates the relation between the human soul and plant powers, explaining why animal power is mentioned before the plant powers.
rows.anchor: Nefs-i insânî ile kuvâ-yı nebâtiye beyninde alâka

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: The harm to the soul is the body’s strengthening of its attachments and prevention of the soul’s fitting nourishment, which consists in encompassing the heavenly and earthly dominion and enduring impressions.
rows.anchor: cevher-i nefse lâzım gelen şer ise onda beden alâikını muhkemleştirmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same interpretation works if the darkening one denotes solid matter or minerals, or if the phrase covers elemental bodies including all three generated kinds and the human body; earlier interpretations branch from it.
rows.anchor: Bazılarının dediği gibi “gāsık” cism-i câmide

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knots may also allude to authority, the pledge of allegiance, or the knot of sovereignty, as in reports from ʿUmar and Ubayy; those reports may reflect this verse.
rows.anchor: هلك اهل العقد ve هلك اهل العقدة gibi velâyet ve akd-i bey‘at

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can portray both rulers tightening the knot through misrule and oppression, and rebels loosening rights through incitement and sedition; both are grave evils for which refuge is required.
rows.anchor: zimamdârânın sû’-i idareleri, câh hırsları, tahakküm ve te‘addî dâ‘iyeleriyle o ukdeleri sıkıştırmak yolundaki zulüm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although knots can carry literal or figurative senses, their core sense is a knot; the phrase does not mean ordinary tying or untying, but is a conventional allusion to magic and thus to sorcerers generally.
rows.anchor: murad tâbirin hakikati üzere düğüme üflemekten ibaret değil, sihirden kinâyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magic should be understood broadly as turning something away from its proper aspect, a sense that encompasses the interpretations just surveyed.
rows.anchor: sihrin herhangi bir şeyi vechinden sarf ve tahvil etmek mânasıyla anlamak muvâfık olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A envier’s evil is realized when he acts on resentment against another’s blessing and begins verbal or practical steps to harm its recipient; while envy stays latent, it does not hurt the target.
rows.anchor: nefsindeki hasedinin muktezâsını fiile çıkarmaya kalkıştığı, mahsûduna karşı kavlen ve fiilen ızrar mebâdîsini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account locates danger when envy boils into hostility and the malicious self turns toward its target; the evil eye commonly occurs at that moment.
rows.anchor: Hased galeyan edip de mahsûduna karşı kin ve gazab ve kasd-ı adâvetle nefs-i habîsini tevcih eylediği vakit

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author depicts malicious glances as sparks that may strike a vulnerable target like lightning, comparing the harm of jealous eyes with the pain caused by snakes’ looks.
rows.anchor: nice hâsidler ve kötü gözlüler vardır ki hased gözüyle baktıkları zaman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a person resists envy instead of acting on it, the target is unharmed and the struggle may earn reward, although the envier continues to harm himself while the feeling persists.
rows.anchor: nefsinde sakladığı ve bu yolda nefsi ile mücahede edebildiği takdirde mahsûda bir şerri dokunmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the restriction to the moment of envy signals the difference between inward feeling and enacted harm; the phrase may also mean the envier’s sin and ugly state when displaying its effects.
rows.anchor: إِذَا حَسَدَ diye takyid buyurulması bu farka işaret için olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak, who created all these dangers and alone protects from them; His protection is promised to those who seek Him sincerely.
rows.anchor: hepsini yaratan ve hepsinin şerrinden koruyacak olan O’dur

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Rāghib defines envy as wishing that a blessing depart from its rightful recipient, often accompanied by striving to remove it; a report contrasts believers’ emulation with hypocrites’ envy.
rows.anchor: Râgıb’ın beyânına göre: “Hased, bir nimetin müstahikkından zevâlini temennidir

rows.speaker: Kāmûs ve sâir
rows.claim: The lexicons define envy broadly, whether or not the envier wants the blessing transferred to himself.
rows.anchor: Kāmûs’un ve sâirenin beyânına göre de o nimetin kendisine tahvîlini isteyip istememekten e‘amdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blameworthy envy means resenting another’s blessing and wishing it removed; translating it simply as jealousy is inaccurate.
rows.anchor: şer olan hasedin asıl mânası başkasında bir nimet görmekten müteezzî olup onun zevâlini istemektir

rows.speaker: Âsım Efendi
rows.claim: In its more proper sense, jealousy is protective zeal or honor about a threat to reputation and chastity, such as a spouse’s fidelity, and is praiseworthy rather than envy.
rows.anchor: Nam ve nâmusa halel verecek hâletten hamiyet eylemek mânasınadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jealousy can sometimes be used metaphorically for envy, but the word is broader and does not always mean blameworthy envy.
rows.anchor: “hased”i sade “kıskanmak” diye terceme etmek doğru değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protective zeal supports flourishing, advancement, moral integrity, defending rights and preserving blessings; exceeding one’s own rights turns it into ignorant fanaticism and envy.
rows.anchor: iffet, hakkın himayesi, nimetin muhafazası onunla hâsıl olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāghib’s qualification that the blessing belongs to a deserving person implies injustice in envy: wishing a usurper to lose stolen goods and restoring them to their owner is justice, not envy.
rows.anchor: bir gāsıbın gasbettiği nimetin zevâlini temenni etmek hased demek olmadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resenting a deserved blessing and wishing its removal is unjust envy; if kept as an inward thought it harms the envier but not the target, while acting to remove it becomes oppression and aggression.
rows.anchor: fiile çıkmayıp hadîs-i nefs kabîlinden kuvvede kaldıkça hâside zararı olursa da başkasına dokunmaz

rows.speaker: İbn Sînâ
rows.claim: Ibn Sīnā reads the envier as the body with animal and plant powers and the envied as the rational soul: the verse describes their conflict.
rows.anchor: İbn Sînâ burada da şöyle demiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward lesson is to turn toward and perfect the spirit, since the human being is truly a spirit rather than a body; seek refuge from bodily appetite and anger that would bury and destroy it.
rows.anchor: Ey nefs-i insânî! Bütün mahlûkātın, bâhusus kevn ü fesad şânından olan maddiyyâtın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura enumerates the evils threatening people in religion and worldly life and promises escape through refuge; the Prophet rejoiced at its revelation and continued seeking refuge with it and the following sura.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah bunlar nâzil olduğu zaman ferahlanmış ve bunlarla te‘avvüze devam buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general phrase “evil of what He created” gathers the sources of harm, while darkness, puffers and envier detail their ranks or chief forms; this sura chiefly treats external or bodily harms.
rows.anchor: مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ isti‘âze olunacak şürûr mebâdîsinin hepsine icmâlen şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse moves from general evils toward human malice, then the following Sūrat al-Nās details inward evils and the stages of the soul seeking refuge, completing the promise and explaining the phrase further.
rows.anchor: Nâs Sûresi ile hitam verilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative or descriptive “mā” in “what He created” may be definite or indefinite; “darkness” and “envier” are indefinite singular, whereas “puffers in knots” is definite plural.
rows.anchor: “Gāsık”, “hâsid” nekre ve müfred, aradaki ٱلنَّفَّٰثَٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ ma‘rife ve cemi‘olarak getirilmiştir

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Râzî
rows.claim: They explain that darkness and envy are indefinite because not every darkening or envious person is evil, and envy can mean beneficial emulation, whereas every knot-blower is evil.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî ve Râzî “zira her gāsık, her hâsid şirrîr değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds that grammatical explanation unclear; it is more evident that generic singulars seek refuge from every darkening force and every envier when acting harmfully.
rows.anchor: Lâkin gāsık ile hâsidin şerri, ekseriya karanlıkta ve mechûliyet içinde tanınmayarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness and envy often work unseen from behind, whereas sorcerers openly smile and whisper their malice; the author likens the darkening one to a sudden bandit and envy to an arsonist.
rows.anchor: Gāsık bir eşkıya gibi ansızın basar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because sorcerers are especially recognizable and notorious for deliberate mischief, the definite plural “the puffers” is best understood with a conventional or generic article; the next sura’s definite “the whisperer” complements it.
rows.anchor: İşte bunlar içinde en ziyade bile bile şerlerine düşülenler neffâseler olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord of people” presents God as their creator and owner who nurtures them from dark, insensible matter into perceptive social beings, develops their reason and duties, and guides them toward good.
rows.anchor: halk ve emriyle insanlar yaratan ve sun‘u kudretiyle o gāsık kara topraktan o duygusuz, muzlim maddeden tan gibi parlayan duygulu insanlar yetiştiren

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “King of people” means the sovereign who governs human faculties by command and prohibition, according to their ranks and divine wisdom, directing them toward ordered good and perfection.
rows.anchor: bütün melekât ve kuvvelerini nizâm-ı hayr ile gāye-i kemâllerine doğru faaliyete sevketmek üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s kingship is absolute and lasting: He gives and removes dominion and can exalt or abase whom He wills.
rows.anchor: dilediğine mülk verip şah yapan, dilediğini de padişah iken indirip atan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God of people” names the true object of worship for mature people who discern truth from falsehood, good from evil and lasting from transient pleasure, and submit their lives and hopes to Him.
rows.anchor: aklî melekeleri tekemmül etmiş; hakkı nâhaktan, hakikati hayâlden, güzeli çirkinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone deserves divinity and has complete power over creation, annihilation, life, death, reward and punishment; He is One and Self-Sufficient.
rows.anchor: ulûhiyet ancak kendinin hakkı olan o Ehad Samed Allah’a sığınırım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord” may be used by relation for beings besides God, and “king” may also apply to others though more specifically; “god” admits no association and belongs truly to God alone, making the terms progressively more specific.
rows.anchor: “Rab” ismi “rabbü’d-dâr” ve “rabbü’l-mâl” gibi izâfetle kullanıldığı zaman Allah’tan mâ‘adâya da söylenebilir

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî ve muhakkıkīn
rows.claim: Although the second and third titles may grammatically be adjectives or substitutes of “Lord,” Zamakhsharī and other rigorous scholars prefer construing them as explanatory appositions.
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî ve sâir muhakkıkīn atf-ı beyan olmalarını ihtiyar eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God is Lord of everything, the sura singles out people because Qur’an’s purpose is human guidance and education; its ending directs attention back to its beginning.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın hikmet-i nüzûlü insanların terbiyesi, insanları sırât-ı müstakīme hidâyet ve irşad olduğu cihetle

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: The formulation teaches a fitting path of refuge: belonging among humankind under God’s care, ownership and servitude increases the causes of mercy and compassion.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud’un beyan ettiği vechile bunda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command to seek this refuge is itself a sign of generosity indicating that He guarantees protection.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın bunu böyle emir buyurması ve bu suretle korumayı kat‘iyyen vaadine delâlet eder delâil-i keremdendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil chiefly concerns Satan, humanity’s known enemy; taking refuge places people in God’s care and servitude against him, as God says Satan has no authority over His sincere servants.
rows.anchor: burada isti‘âze olunan şer bilhassa insanlara adâvet ile mâruf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge as one person within the perfected community of worship is more eloquent than speaking only as an individual: it praises encompassing power and mercy, shares others’ blessings, expresses gratitude and avoids selfishness; communal prayer is more virtuous.
rows.anchor: öyle demekten daha beliğdir. Çünkü insanlık merâtibinin en mütekâmil saffı bulunan ilâhîler saffında ehlullah cemaati içinde

rows.speaker: Beyzâvî ve bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: They explain the phrase’s restriction to people by saying the evil sought against is specific to human souls.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî gibi bazı müfessirîn بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ diye tahsîsin nüktesi burada isti‘âze olunan vesvese şerrinin nüfûs-ı insâniyeye mahsus bir şer olduğunu söylemekle iktifâ etmişlerse

rows.speaker: Sâhib-Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains the repeated “people” as required by appositional clarification: clarification uses explicit expression rather than a pronoun.
rows.anchor: Sâhib-Keşşâf bunu atf-ı beyan olmasının îcâbına hamlederek demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī adds that repetition honors humanity: God identifies Himself at the scripture’s close as people’s Lord, King and God, implying they are the noblest creatures.
rows.anchor: Râzî bununla beraber “bir de” der, “bu tekrar insanların şerefini artırmayı iktizâ eyler
